_what_this_is: Every version of restore.sh, the escape hatch, that has existed in this project, listed by the sha256 of the script itself. From nest format 2.3 on, a copy of the script travels inside every nest at .renest/escape/restore.sh, and that copy is frozen: fixes made later never reach it. This table is how you tell which copy you are holding.
_how_to_use: sha256sum .renest/escape/restore.sh inside your nest, then find that hash below. known_issues lists what was wrong with that copy and fixed later.
_an_empty_issue_list_means: No issue has been recorded against that version -- not that it is known to have none. Only issues we found and fixed appear here.

known_issues.summary: A stalled download was never given up on, so the script could hang indefinitely instead of failing.
A leftover failure record from an earlier run made a fully successful run report itself as failed.
Dependency sources of the form git+https:// were judged untrusted and refused, so nests using several of the most common extensions could not be rebuilt.
Code carried inside the nest itself was treated as an outside server, so fine-tuning nests could not be rebuilt at all.
On a machine short of a system library, the closing line saying so was covered up by the Done line above it.
The C library version was not checked, so a nest packed on a newer system passed every byte check on an older one and then crashed on first start.
Presigned download links were printed in full in the script's own output, including on the success path.
When a rebuild failed, the output explaining why only flashed past the screen instead of being kept.
Said nothing when the machine's processor lacked instructions the environment needs.
Said nothing when the target machine was a different processor family than the one the nest was packed on; the failure surfaced only after the whole download.
Three defects at once: wrong bytes were left in place instead of being removed, a failed install command was not reported, and a material file whose name contains a space produced a wrong error.
After a rebuild it never said which of your own material files you have to put back yourself.
On machines that are not Linux it raised a string of alarms that did not apply.
